Subject: Data residency confirmation + SIG/CAIQ artifacts for EU pilot

Hi Jonas (and Ben),

We’re putting the final compliance checklist together for our EU pilot and need a short formal confirmation that Redwood will only serve EU region nodes for Shoreline’s pilot work and that private VPC endpoints will be used for inference traffic. The security team asked specifically for: SOC 2 scope summary, SIG/CAIQ mapping, and a network diagram showing VPC peering and egress controls.

Can you send a bundle we can drop into our procurement/security review? If you can include any signed commitment language (even a one-page letter) that would speed approvals.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Elena
Elena Moretti
Director, Cloud Security | Shoreline Health

Attachments: none

Subject: Re: Data residency confirmation + SIG/CAIQ artifacts for EU pilot

Elena — thanks for the note.

Short answer: yes, we can commit to hosting the production pilot traffic in EU-only nodes and will provision a dedicated private endpoint (VPC peering / PrivateLink) for Shoreline. We’ll include an evidence pack that maps SOC 2 exhibits to SIG control families and a CAIQ slice that highlights the controls relevant to data residency and network isolation.

I’m looping in Irene (security) to assemble the artifacts and Ben (solutions) to validate the topology diagram. We’ll target delivery by EOD Mon (Aug 3) so your procurement team has time for review.

Planned attachments in the pack: redwood_soc2-summary.pdf, caiq_mapping_sheet.xlsx, vpc_network_diagram.png, and a one-page residency_commitment_letter.docx.

If there’s any non-standard contractual language you need (SLA change, breach notification timing, or data center exceptions), flag it now and we’ll route to legal.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Solutions & Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Following up with the artifact list and a short explanation of what each file demonstrates: 

1) redwood_soc2-summary.pdf — condensed SOC 2 scope & exhibits (in-scope services: inference runtime, control plane for the Private deployment). Includes control IDs we use for data handling and incident response.

2) caiq_mapping_sheet.xlsx — CAIQ/SIG rows we extract for residency & network isolation. We’ve highlighted responses for Data Location, Logical Isolation, Operator Access, and Key Management. Note: some SIG items reference third-party operator inventories; we’ve included a redacted operator roster where relevant.

3) vpc_network_diagram.png — a high-level diagram showing: dedicated EU node cluster, VPC peering name (redwood-shoreline-prod-peer), private endpoint IP ranges, NAT/egress guards, and where HSM/KMS calls are routed (eu-kms-1). The diagram explicitly marks egress guardrails — no public egress from inference nodes except to KMS and telemetry endpoints over TLS.

4) residency_commitment_letter.docx — one-page commitment we can sign: confirms (a) EU-only hosting for pilot, (b) private endpoint requirement, (c) retention window options and data deletion processes, and (d) notification timing for any planned cross-region failover.

Operational notes / clarifications:
- Failover: we can offer regional-only failover within EU zones; cross-border (EU->US) failover requires an explicit acceptance step and authorized contacts.
- Keys: customer-managed CMK via our KMS integration is supported; if you supply a key in an EU KMS partition we will not export key material out of EU.
- Logs: audit logs for the pilot will be streamed to your SIEM via the private peering (sample format and retention options in the SOC 2 PDF).

I’ve uploaded the pack to our shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_shoreline-evidence (link below). If you need a CAIQ PDF rather than the spreadsheet slice, say so and we’ll generate it.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Security Architect | Redwood Inference
